coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Pier 70 Building 14
record.summary: A World War II double-gable corrugated-metal heavy warehouse east of the Machine Shop, framing the Historic Core's plaza with Building 2; the smallest of Orton's eight Historic Core buildings, rehabilitated with a new mezzanine and seismic bracing (certificate of occupancy August 2017) and subleased whole to Obscura Digital (The Madison Square Garden Company) for seven years from September 2017.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL, surveyed building footprint (DataSF Building Footprints) -- high confidence in the outline itself and its match to Building 14: position matches Figure 6.4.2's own label (39m away, the closest and only plausible candidate among the lot's other footprint pieces once 113/114/115/116's own pieces are excluded) and its area independently matches the previously-cited 16,315 GSF within 3%. As with the other buildings split from oversized Assessor lots this project, the match rests on position and size, not an explicit building-number attribute in the footprint dataset itself (no such attribute exists there).
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Building Footprints dataset (real, surveyed building outline; not tied to an Assessor parcel).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: This structure has no street address in DataSF's Assessor roll and sits on the same huge, largely-unsubdivided Assessor lot (blklot 4052001) as Buildings 101/102/104/113-116/21 and other structures across central Pier 70 -- no distinct blklot exists to join for Building 14 specifically, so this feature uses the real building footprint instead, matched individually.
notes.regulatory_context: Building 14, a basic heavy warehouse dated to 1941 (per the 2013 HPC packet, 2013.1168E) with approximately 16,000 GSF of space and a 66 foot height, sits immediately east of the Union Iron Works Machine Shop complex (Buildings 113/114/115/116), framing a shared courtyard with them per the D4D's rehabilitation concept. Rehabbed by Orton Development Inc. (ODI) as part of the same 20th Street Historic Core project; proposed for the same industrial/warehouse/maker-space use (food, tech, life science, biotech, education, arts production) with ancillary office, showroom, and retail as its neighbors.

facts.value: Orton Development, Inc. through Historic Pier 70, LLC (66-year master lease L-15814 from the Port of San Francisco)

Contributing resource to the Union Iron Works Historic District (NRHP, listed April 17, 2014)
1941 (NRHP nomination); 1944 per the 2013 HPC packet and the Port's 2019 memo
140 ft by 116 ft 6 in by 66 ft tall, double-gable metal building clad in corrugated galvanized iron, with a 20-ton crane
15,969 (NRHP); 16,315 before and 25,215 after rehabilitation (Port); 23,000 sq ft per the contractor
Marcy Wong Donn Logan Architects; IwamotoScott (contractor's credit)
Full interior and exterior renovation, new mezzanine, seismic bracing, restrooms, kitchen and office spaces, and a light-industrial workshop for a digital production company
Obscura Digital / The Madison Square Garden Company (entire building, from September 2017, seven-year term)
Heavy warehouse; storage for the Port's maintenance division before rehabilitation
Forms a courtyard with Building 2 and the 113/114/115/116 complex; the ~45,000 sq ft plaza is publicly accessible
